It generates a ~40MB db and times json.load, JSONStorage.read, db.all(), and cached/uncached search to show where read time goes, as part of read-performance work.

Design constraint for any future read cache: the user's db files live on an NFS share with 1-second mtime resolution, and a previous mtime-based cache (last year) was removed because it served stale data when the importer wrote twice within one second. mtime or mtime+size validation is therefore untrustworthy. No approach is chosen yet (user to decide); options listed: content hash validation, per-process cache invalidated on write(), opt-in JSONStorage(..., cache=True), and fewer redundant reads per operation. Caveat: Table returns cached dicts that callers can mutate.

items.text: Read-path architecture: JSONStorage.read() re-reads and re-parses the whole file on every call, and Table._read_table() calls it on every operation. On a 43 MB db (180k docs, Nov 2026 benchmark) a new-query search() takes ~516 ms (about 96% JSON parse, ~50 ms condition evaluation), db.all() ~978 ms (half parse, half building Document objects), len(db) ~468 ms, and a repeated query ~0 ms. Repeated queries are served from Table._query_cache, but get, contains, all and len bypass the cache.

items.text: The Table class was reworked between Jan and Feb 2020 to simplify the API and clarify method semantics: it stores the next ID instead of the last ID, `Table.contains` accepts only a single doc ID (list semantics were ambiguous), `process_docs` was removed, `len(table)` performance improved, and default cache capacity and default table name became configurable. Follow-up fixes covered ID generation, `len(db)` on empty DBs, and doc ID conversion in updates.
Internal type checks were refactored from isinstance-dict to isinstance-Mapping (Claus Aichinger, Oct 2018), so any Mapping is accepted rather than only dict.

Atomic writes to avoid data corruption on crashes were added (#468, Stefano Scafiti) in May 2022, then reverted by Markus Siemens after the feature broke CI (GitHub run 6561403728). A Windows atomic-write support fix was also committed. CI was expanded to macOS and Windows, with Windows+PyPy3 and macOS+PyPy3 excluded.

In Oct 2026 docs and type hints were aligned with runtime behavior (#644, fixes #630): Query.test typing, operations.add accepting str, usage.rst fixes, Table.get docstring, and Query.search flags being passed to re.search.

items.text: TinyDB v4.0 (Nov 2019) was a major architecture refactor to modernize and simplify the codebase (#284, closes #250 and #103): Python 2 support removed, ujson support deprecated, the deprecated element ID API removed, project configuration switched to Poetry, and type annotations added.

Table.get gained a doc_ids parameter (feat 6f03ec6, see #504, closes #486) allowing multiple documents to be fetched by ID in one call, followed by documentation of Table.get(doc_ids=[...]) (b8ffbfe), May-June 2023.

Query behavior fixes in TinyDB (Oct 2026): Query.any/all no longer treat str/bytes/bytearray as sequences (they use collections.abc.Sequence; #641, fixes #638), and regex flags are now part of the matches/search query hash so case-insensitive and case-sensitive searches no longer share a query-cache entry (#640, fixes #637). Both prevent incorrect matches and query-cache poisoning.
